04 · Typography

Arial / Helvetica for screen; DejaVu Sans as cross-platform render target for matplotlib and ReportLab.

Document Type Scale

RoleSizeWeight

Document figures vs projected figures. The sizes above apply to figures rendered at document scale — print, PDF, web, and on-screen reading at 60–80 cm. Figures embedded in projected slides follow the projection minimums in §11 (body 18 pt, heading 28 pt, axis labels 18 pt). A 9 pt tick label that reads fine on a laptop disappears from the back row of a conference room.

05 · Figure Standards

Every figure has a visible hierarchy: title → axes → data → annotation. Axis furniture is rendered in neutral.200–neutral.300 so it reads as structure, not content.

Neutrals default, Brand Blue highlights. Most elements draw from the neutral ramp; Brand Blue or Blue 400–700 is reserved for the one or two elements that matter most.

Layout

ParameterValue
Aspect ratioMatch to the data, not the canvas. Categorical comparisons tolerate squarer ratios (4:3 or 3:2); trend data is banked so the mean slope sits near 45° (Cleveland). Do not stretch or squash to fill slide real estate — the resulting slope change distorts the reader's reading of rate.
SpinesLeft + bottom only
GridlinesHorizontal, neutral.200, 0.5 pt, dashed
Data line width1.8–2.2 pt primary; 1.0–1.6 pt secondary
Markers5–6 pt filled circles; white outline on colored fills
Resolution300 dpi PNG + SVG/PDF vector

Figure Integrity

These rules govern what a figure is allowed to claim visually. Violating any of them misrepresents the data, regardless of how well-styled the figure looks.

RuleSpecification
Zero baseline on bar chartsBars encode quantity by length; a truncated y-axis inflates differences. If a y-axis truncation is unavoidable (tight effect on a large background), switch to a dot plot or Cleveland dot plot rather than a truncated bar.
Log scales labeled as suchAxis title reads log10 concentration (nM) or equivalent, with one tick per decade as the base case. Never a silent log transform.
Uncertainty is shownCaption CI endpoints, at-risk / n-per-arm tables, inline error markers, or individual points overlaid on summary statistics. Shaded CI bands on line plots are not the default — they are drawn only on explicit user request. Bar definition (SD, SEM, or 95% CI) is stated on-figure in the caption or legend — not left to the reader to guess.
No 3D effects on 2D data3D bars, 3D pies, and drop shadows distort perceived area and introduce perspective error. Flat, 2D, always.
No rainbow / jet colormaps on continuous dataRainbow has no perceptual ordering, introduces false luminance bands, and fails both CVD and grayscale. Use viridis-family or the §06 divergent cycle for continuous scalars.
No category encoded by hue aloneCombine color with shape (circle / square / triangle), line style, or direct label, so the encoding survives grayscale printing, low-quality projection, and color vision deficiency.
Isotype charts replicate 1:1To show a 5:1 ratio, draw five icons beside one icon — never one icon scaled 5× larger. Scaling a single icon by height inadvertently scales area and visually overstates the difference (the area-vs-height scaling error).
No dual y-axes without justificationDual y-axes invite spurious visual correlation between series scaled independently. Reach for small multiples or a twin-panel layout first.

06 · Scientific Data Visualization

Two decision rules make every chart color choice deterministic. Rule 1 selects the cycle based on the data's categorical structure. Rule 2 selects the ramp step based on each mark's visual role.

Rule 1 · Choose the Cycle

If your data is…Use cycleRationale
Two arms, one carries the narrative (treatment vs control)Cycle 1 · Treatment/ControlSame-hue pair with lightness hierarchy
N arms, one carries the narrative answerCycle 2 · FocusThree background arms + one promoted focus
N arms, all equal weight — no focusCycle 2 · PeerBlue ramp at stepped lightness; no promotion
Signed / directional effects (up vs down, gain vs loss)Cycle 3 · OpposingBlue + Orange paired across the ramp
Continuous signed scalar (heatmap z-scores)Cycle 3 · DivergentBlue 700 → white → Orange 700
3–4 categories with one conceptual outlierCycle 4 · Multi-CategoryStep-spaced Blue + Orange for outlier
The Focus-vs-Peer branch. Before reaching for Cycle 2, ask: does any arm carry the narrative answer? If yes, use Focus. If no, use Peer. Never promote an arm arbitrarily just because the palette has a focus slot — the v2.0 Cycle 2 implicitly assumed promotion was always available, which was wrong.

Cycle 1 · Treatment / Control

brand.blue tx
blue.300 ctrl
CI bands (on user request only): matching-hue @ α=0.18
Two-arm studies. Same-hue palette with lightness doing the hierarchy work — treatment at saturated Brand Blue, control as a lighter tint of the same hue. Supersedes v2.0's Blue-versus-gray pairing.

Cycle 2 · Peer

blue.800/600/400/200 (4 arms)
blue.700/500/300 (3 arms)
Equal-weight peer comparisons where no arm carries the narrative. Lightness distinguishes without ranking. Good default for sibling siRNAs, cell lines, dose levels where ordering is arbitrary.

Cycle 2 · Focus

blue.500/300/200 receding
+ focus variant below
N arms with one promoted. Three background arms in receding Blue, focus arm in one of three intensity options:
Orange 500Default. Saturated hue contrast. Use when focus arm is categorically different.
Orange 400Softer. Less saturated; focus present but quieter.
Blue 800Monochromatic. Dark lightness alone. Use when focus is "more of the same" rather than different in kind (e.g., highest dose in a dose-response).

Cycle 3 · Opposing

blue.600 negative
orange.600 positive
Signed or directional data. Avoids red/green colorblind confusion. Divergent heatmaps extend to blue.700 → white → orange.700.

Cycle 4 · Multi-Category

blue.800/500/300 + orange.500
3–4 categories with one conceptually distinct (e.g., vehicle vs compounds). If all categories are peers, use Cycle 2 · Peer instead.

Rule 2 · Choose the Ramp Step

StepRoleWhere
50 – 200Fills, tints, surfacesBox fills, callout backgrounds, matching-hue CI bands when drawn on user request
300Light data strokesCycle 1 control, Cycle 2 Focus receding arms
400Primary dataDefault for lines and markers
500 – 600Emphasis / button fillsCTAs, hover states
700Text, borders, linksAxis titles on light theme; heatmap extremes
800 – 900Dark page, deepest contrastDark theme bg; monochromatic Focus promotion

Worked Examples

Kaplan–Meier Survival

Cycle 1 · Treatment/Control

Two-arm trial with treatment as narrative subject. Treatment in Brand Blue; control in Blue 300 — same hue family, lightness hierarchy. No CI bands on the plot by default; day-120 95% CI endpoints are reported in the annotation and a numbers-at-risk table sits beneath the x-axis.

treatment · brand.blue control · blue.300 no CI bands · at-risk table

Volcano Plot

Cycle 3 · Opposing

Signed effect size. Down-regulated in Blue 600, up-regulated in Orange 600, non-significant in Neutral 300. Avoids red/green.

down · blue.600 up · orange.600 n.s. · neutral.300

Dose–Response

Cycle 4 · Multi-Category

Three compounds + one vehicle control. Blue ramp steps preserve hue identity across compounds; Orange 500 tags the conceptually distinct vehicle.

A · blue.800 B · blue.500 C · blue.300 vehicle · orange.500

Divergent Heatmap

Cycle 3 · Divergent

Z-scored expression values. Colormap interpolates Blue 700 → white → Orange 700 in linear sRGB. Matched lightness curves on both ramps keep perceptual distance from zero symmetric.

−z · blue.700 0 · white +z · orange.700

Tumor Volume Time-Course

Cycle 1 · Treatment/Control

Treatment in Brand Blue; vehicle in Blue 300. No CI bands on the plot by default; day-28 95% CI endpoints are reported in the annotation. Dose-administration arrows sit below the x-axis in Neutral 700.

Immune Cell Populations (Box + Strip)

Four populations × two conditions. Box fills use Blue ramp 200 (lighter condition) and 500 (darker). Median lines in Neutral 900. Jittered points at 50% opacity of fill.

08 · Accessibility & Compliance

Palette is validated against WCAG 2.1 Level AA. Blue and Orange ramps share Oklch lightness curves, so simulated-colorblind rendering preserves the blue-orange axis as a dark-light differential under deuteranopia and protanopia.

Checklist

Before publishing a figure:
  1. Grayscale version still interpretable.
  2. No category encoded by hue alone — shape, line style, or label also distinguishes.
  3. All text ≥ 9 pt at rendered size, AA contrast verified.
  4. Exported as 300 dpi PNG + vector (SVG/PDF).
  5. Cycle documented in caption or YAML metadata.
  6. Alt text describes the finding, not the chart type. Write "Bar chart shows a 2-fold increase in cell viability for the treatment group" — not "image of a bar chart."

09 · Voice & Messaging

Oligon sounds like a clinical-stage biotech run by scientists who trust their audience — confident without bravado, technical without jargon theater. This section governs copy across every medium: web, deck, social, email, and spoken scripts.

Positioning

Oligon develops next-generation RNAi therapeutics. The SeekR™ platform integrates two RNA aptamers (targeting) flanking two siRNA silencers (payload) into a single self-delivering drug. The elevator pitch lives at the intersection of three ideas: modular, precise, programmable.

Voice Rules

Rule 1 · Translate, Don't Dumb Down

Introduce every technical term with a plain-language analog in the same breath. Never strip the term; never leave the term unexplained. The glossary in §10 is the canonical pairing bank.

DO

Aptamers — RNA oligos that function like chemical antibodies — selectively bind target proteins.

DON'T

Our SELEX-selected aptamers exhibit high-affinity binding to cognate surface epitopes.

Rule 2 · Numbers Over Adjectives

Specific figures carry credibility. "Tenfold" beats "significant." "$14M seed" beats "well-funded." Readers in pharma have heard every adjective.

DO

About a tenfold improvement in cellular internalization.

DON'T

A revolutionary breakthrough in drug delivery.

Rule 3 · Verbs Over Nouns

Active voice with specific verbs. "Reprograms pathogenic T cells" beats "offers T-cell reprogramming solutions." Nominalization deadens scientific claims.

DO

SeekR bridges drive selective and potent siRNA uptake.

DON'T

The SeekR platform delivers targeted therapeutic intervention solutions.

Messaging Pillars

Four claims every major asset should trace to at least one of. An asset without a pillar anchor is probably off-mission.

PillarClaimEvidence to cite
Self-deliveringSystemic injection, no special formulation.Platform architecture.
Multi-modalDual aptamers + dual siRNA in one molecule.SeekR structure diagram.
Multi-targetingBivalent binding enables receptor cross-linking.~10× internalization gain.
Any cell typeWorks in T cells, cancer cells, and beyond.Pipeline breadth — six programs.

10 · Copy Patterns

Four repeatable patterns cover most copy work: the eyebrow + headline pair, three headline formulas, the CTA language bank, and the technical-to-plain glossary. Reach for these before inventing new patterns.

Eyebrow + Headline Pattern

The most distinctive structural move in the system. Uses §04 Typography directly — the eyebrow is an H3 (14 pt uppercase, 700, neutral.900, 0.05em letter-spacing), the headline is an H1 or H2 depending on hierarchy. A 6–10 pt vertical gap binds them as a unit.

Eyebrow rules. One to three words. Categorical, not a sub-headline (THERAPEUTICS, SCIENTIFIC APPROACH, PIPELINE UPDATE — not "Our approach to therapeutics"). Color at neutral.900 on light surfaces, neutral.50 on dark. Never Brand Blue — that is reserved for logos and Cycle 1 treatment per §03 and §06.

Headline Formulas

Formula A · Platform Claim

[Platform or molecule] [verb] [outcome] [in or for context].

SeekR bridges drive selective and potent siRNA uptake.

Formula B · Capability Statement

[Outcome noun] for [audience or use].

Dual binders for precision in delivery.

Formula C · Eyebrow + Answer

[Category eyebrow] / [declarative answer].

THE TECHNOLOGICAL BREAKTHROUGH

The bivalent SeekR bridge drives selective and potent siRNA uptake.

Sentence case everywhere. "The bivalent SeekR bridge drives selective..." — not "The Bivalent SeekR Bridge Drives Selective...". Brand terms preserve their casing: SeekR, RNAi, siRNA, DNA, RNA.

CTA Language Bank

Use these. Nothing else. Consistency across assets is the point.

CTAWhen to use
Learn moreInternal pipeline links, news articles
Explore [topic]Platform and pipeline sections
Contact usPartnership, investor, or press inquiries
Read the paperLinking to preprints and publications
Watch the videoEmbedded or linked video content
Avoid. "Click here", "Get started", "Book a demo" (this is not SaaS), "Unlock", "Discover" (overused industry-wide).

Technical-to-Plain Glossary

Use the same pairing twice so readers see it reinforced. When a term appears in a headline, the pairing belongs in the nearest body paragraph.

Technical termPlain translation
AptamerRNA oligo that functions like a chemical antibody
siRNARNA silencer that switches off a specific gene
SeekRA single drug molecule carrying targeting binders and silencers
EndocytosisThe process cells use to pull material inside
Receptor cross-linkingBinding two receptors at once to force them into the cell
T-cell exhaustionWhen cancer-fighting immune cells lose their ability to function
BivalentBinding at two sites at once
RNAiThe cellular pathway that silences specific genes

Presentations

Investor & Scientific Deck Structure

Slide typeSpecification
Coverblue.900 full-bleed; H3 eyebrow (e.g. INVESTOR UPDATE — Q2 2026); H1 title (28 pt); wordmark bottom-right
Section dividerblue.900; H3 eyebrow + H1 only, no body
Content slideWhite ground; H3 eyebrow + H2 title; content area
Data slideWhite ground; H3 eyebrow + H2 title; figure per §05–§06 at 300 dpi
Quote slideblue.900; oversized quotation mark in Brand Blue at 0.25 opacity; display-size quote; attribution
Closing / contactblue.900; CTA text; wordmark; contact email
Projection typography minimums. Body 18 pt, heading 28 pt, axis labels on embedded figures 18 pt. Never use caption size (11 pt per §04) on projected slides; if a data figure's axis labels are below 18 pt at projected scale, relabel them natively in PowerPoint or scale the figure up before exporting.
Figure integration. Data figures come from matplotlib or ggplot2 per §05 and §06. Do not re-style them inside PowerPoint — export at 300 dpi PNG or SVG and drop in. The unified Arial / DejaVu Sans typography (§04) means figures render consistently alongside slide titles.

Slide-Title Headline Rule

Make the slide title a full-sentence declarative takeaway, not a topic label. The title should carry the finding in words so a reader who never hears the presenter can reconstruct the argument from titles alone. This is the deck-scale instance of the §09 voice rules (numbers over adjectives, verbs over nouns) and the §10 Formula A copy pattern.

DO

SeekR bridges drive ~10× siRNA uptake in Jurkat T cells.

DON'T

Jurkat uptake data.
Exceptions. Reference slides, disclosure slides, acknowledgments, and appendix raw-data slides carry neutral topic labels. Agenda and section-divider slides carry an eyebrow-only pattern per §10.

Persistent Footer & Confidentiality

Every content slide after the cover carries footer content set at the Slide Master so it cannot be removed on individual slides. Exact content varies by audience.

Deck audienceFooter lineSlide number
Investor / BDConfidential — Do Not Distribute, neutral.600, 10 ptBottom-right, neutral.600, 10 pt
Scientific Advisory BoardConfidential — SAB use only, optional per-advisor watermark at neutral.200Bottom-right, neutral.600, 10 pt
Conference / seminarEmbargo line if data is pre-publication; otherwise emptyBottom-right, neutral.600, 10 pt
KOL / medical educationMLR job code in the format US-OLIGON-123456 MM/YYYY with expiration dateBottom-right, neutral.600, 10 pt
Internal reviewDocument control line with version and date if regulated; otherwise emptyBottom-right, neutral.600, 10 pt
Set at the master. Footer text placed on individual slides will drift — a collaborator will delete or overwrite it. Enter the footer via Insert > Header & Footer applied to all slides, or edit the Slide Master directly. Apply Home > Reset to any slide where the footer has disappeared.

12 · Asset Specs & File Naming

Naming conventions and delivery expectations for every asset produced under this guide. Keep the conventions strict — downstream search, versioning, and handoff depend on them.

File Naming

Pattern: oligon_[asset-type]_[topic]_[variant]_v[N]_[YYYY-MM].[ext]

The v[N] segment is required. Iterate by bumping v1 → v2 → v3 and preserve prior versions until explicitly retired — never overwrite a prior version, even for changes that feel trivial. Year-month alone cannot disambiguate two iterations in the same month.

ExampleAsset type
oligon_social_seekr-mechanism_li-square_v1_2026-04.pngLinkedIn square social tile
oligon_deck_investor-q1_master_v3_2026-04.pptxInvestor presentation, third iteration
oligon_landing_ctla4-program_hero_v2_2026-04.jpgLanding page hero image, second iteration
oligon_email_aimed25-invite_html_v1_2026-04.htmlEmail funnel asset
oligon_figure_km-survival_fig3_v1_2026-04.svgScientific figure per §05–§06

Required Source Files

Every asset delivered under this guide should ship with:

  1. The final rendered output (.png / .pdf / .mp4)
  2. Editable source (.figma / .psd / .indd / .pptx / .html)
  3. A one-line token manifest stating which §03 semantic tokens and §04 type roles the asset consumes
